newsitem.title: GREECE: OECD sees Greek 97 inflation at 6pct, fiscal laxity.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Greek 97 inflation at 6pct, fiscal laxity.

text.p: Greek inflation will fall to an average 6.0 percent in 1997 from 8.5 percent in 1996, mainly due to the central bank's stable exchange rate policy but the ambitious 4.2 percent of GDP budget deficit target will be overshot, OECD said.

"The principal factor behind the projected reduction in inflation will remain the firm exchange rate policy, which will nevertheless continue to have an adverse impact on the current account and output growth," said the OECD in its economic outlook report on Greece.

But the sharp drop in inflation with the ensuing fall in interest rates has boosted consumer and business confidence, which, coupled with inflows from the European Union, have increased aggregate demand, sped up output growth and stabilised unemployment, it said.
GDP is projected to grow 3.0 percent in 1997 versus 2.6 percent in 1996 and the unemployment rate to be flat at 10.4 percent, the report said.
The official GDP growth projection for this year is 3.5 percent.

Noting that an EU-approved change in accounting practices helped the 1996 general government budget deficit drop to 7.4 percent of GDP from 9.2 percent in 1996, it forecast a 1997 budget deficit of 5.2 percent of GDP against an official target of 4.2 percent.
The report said that a lower than projected GDP growth rate and a slower revenue growth will account for the larger budget deficit.

The main risks were a slippage in fiscal consolidation that could undermine business confidence, higher than projected wage growth and the exchange rate policy which could hurt corporate profits and investments, it added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
